newsitem.title: UK: London precious metals firm on short covering.
newsitem.headline: London precious metals firm on short covering.

text.p: A short covering rally in the Far East boosted precious metals prices by the European start of business on Tuesday, dealers said.
"It all happened by eight o'clock. Since then it's been pretty quiet," one dealer said of the rally which focused on platinum and palladium but also urged gold slightly higher.
Gold was fixed at $346.00 per ounce up from $344.10 on Monday when trading was especially light due to the President's Day holiday closure of the U.S. markets.
Dealers said gold had firmed by around $2.00 since its close and looked the better for breaching resistance at $345.00.
"It could try for $347.00 now or even $348/$349.00 is feasible," one dealer said.
He reasoned that attempts to push the price down had failed and the charts showed underlying strength. These issues together had encouraged the short covering rally.

Figures released by the London Bullion Market Association (LBMA) on Monday showed average daily turnover cleared by LBMA members at 37.2 million ounces in January compared to 29.80 million ounces in December.

"The turnover figures show that January was an exceptional month. For the gold price it was the worst January since 1981 caused by forward selling, fund selling and possibly central bank selling," said precious metal market analyst Andy Smith at Union Bank of Switzerland.
Platinum and palladium recovered from recent profit-taking on covering and fresh buying as dealers mulled the lack of progress on supply contract talks between Russia and Japan.
Seen as complicating the issue a Norilsk spokesman saying that Russia's major platinum group metal producer wanted to sell its output direct to overseas customers.
However an official of Almaz the export agency said on Tuesday he hoped talks would begin this month or next.
Palladium was indicated at $135.00/$136.00, up $2.00 and off an early high of $137.00 bid. Sponge grade material was "non existent" in the market, one dealer said.
Platinum was at $368.50/$369.50, around its highest of the year and $5.00 up on the close. Dealers said platinum was benefiting also from premium trading against gold.
Silver was four cents up at $5.24/$5.26.
